name: ADC122S021CIMM_NOPB
title: ADC122S021: two-channel 12-bit SAR ADC, specified from 50 ksps to 200 ksps, serial interface, VSSOP-8
summary: A 12-bit successive-approximation converter with a two-input multiplexer (IN1, IN2), a built-in sample-and-hold and a four-wire serial port (CS, SCLK, DIN, DOUT) that works with SPI, QSPI, MICROWIRE and DSP ports. Its performance is guaranteed across a range of rates, 50 ksps to 200 ksps with SCLK from 0.8 MHz to 3.2 MHz, rather than at one rate. One supply, 2.7 V to 5.25 V, powers it and is also its reference, so full scale is VA; results are straight binary. It draws 2.2 mW typical at 3.6 V and 7.9 mW at 5.25 V while converting and shuts down while CS is high. The package is an 8-lead VSSOP (DGK), rated for -40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: 0.8 MHz to 3.2 MHz specified; 50 kHz to 16 MHz functional
2.7 V to 5.25 V; VA is the reference
2.2 mW typ at 3.6 V, 7.9 mW typ at 5.25 V; 0.14 µW / 0.32 µW shut down

notes: CIMM order codes ship 1000 to a reel and CIMMX codes 3500 to a reel.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active low. A falling edge starts a conversion, and conversions repeat for as long as it stays low. DOUT is high-impedance and the part powers down while it is high.

pins.name: VA
pins.function: Supply, +2.7 V to +5.25 V, and the conversion reference. Wants a quiet source, bypassed to GND by 1 µF plus a 0.1 µF ceramic within 1 cm of the pin.

pins.name: IN1
pins.function: Analog input 1, 0 V to VA; the channel converted first after power-up.

pins.name: DIN
pins.function: Serial data in: the control register, which picks the next channel, is shifted in on rising SCLK edges.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.function: Serial data out: the result is shifted out on falling SCLK edges, MSB first.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Paces both the conversion and the data transfer.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: An LP2950 low-dropout regulator makes a dedicated VA rail from 5 V. Its input has 1 µF and 0.1 µF to ground; its output, next to the converter, has a 1 µF tantalum and a 0.1 µF. The supply is the converter's reference, so a separate regulator keeps other circuits' noise out of the result; with so little supply current, a precision reference may power VA instead. IN1 and IN2 are the analog inputs, and the four serial lines (SCLK, CS, DIN, DOUT) go to a host microprocessor or DSP.
notes: U3's pins carry the names of the converter pins they drive or read.

operation.text: A successive-approximation converter around a charge-redistribution DAC. While tracking, one switch ties the sampling capacitor through the multiplexer to the chosen input and another balances the comparator; this state covers SCLK cycles 1 to 3 counted from the CS falling edge. To hold, the capacitor is switched to ground, keeping the sampled charge, and the logic adds fixed charge steps from the DAC until the comparator balances; the DAC code then is the result. Hold and conversion run from the 4th to the 16th SCLK cycle.

A frame lasts from CS falling to CS rising and must contain 16, 32, 48 ... rising SCLK edges, one conversion per 16. DOUT is high-impedance with CS high and driven with CS low, so CS also enables the output. The result leaves DOUT MSB first from clock 5 on, behind four leading zeros. With several conversions in one frame, tracking restarts on the SCLK falling edge after rising edge N×16 and hold/convert starts on falling edge N×16+4.
In each conversion the first 8 rising SCLK edges after CS falls clock the control register in at DIN. Its ADD bits choose the input for the next conversion rather than the one under way.

SCLK is gated off inside while CS is high. If SCLK is parked low, CS falling makes an internal falling clock edge, which the converter counts as the first and starts tracking on. If SCLK is parked high, tracking starts on the first SCLK falling edge after CS falls. When CS and SCLK fall closer together than tCSU and tCLH, DIN capture can begin one clock late, so those minimums should be met.
No start-up delay or dummy conversion is needed: the first conversion after power-up is a full one, and it converts IN1.
Output is straight binary with transitions midway between whole LSB values. 1 LSB is VA/4096; the first transition is at VA/8192 and the top one at VA − 1.5 LSB.

VA is the reference, so supply noise reaches the result. A dedicated linear regulator, or enough decoupling from other circuits, keeps VA quiet; the supply current is low enough that a precision reference can power the part. The bypass network sits close to the VA pin.

Each input looks like about 3 pF of pin capacitance, then about 500 Ω of on-resistance in the mux and sampling switch, then the 30 pF sampling capacitor, with ESD diodes to VA and GND. An input more than 300 mV above VA or below GND turns those diodes on and can upset operation, so they are not to be used as signal clamps. A low-impedance source avoids distortion from charging the sampling capacitor, which matters most for AC signals; filtering ahead of the input (low-pass or band-pass) lowers harmonics and noise.
DOUT cannot swing above VA. The digital inputs do not latch up, and the three logic inputs may see signals ahead of VA without latch-up risk, though that order is not recommended.

With CS low the part is fully on and with CS high fully off; it also switches itself off from the 16th falling clock edge of a conversion until the first falling edge of the following one. Back-to-back conversions continue as long as CS stays low, each taking 16 SCLK cycles, so continuous throughput is fSCLK/16. Running SCLK at 3.2 MHz and converting less often, with shutdown between conversions, trades rate for power.

Charging the DOUT load draws current pulses from VA, and discharging it dumps current into the resistive substrate as ground bounce; both cost SNR and SINAD, more so the bigger the load. Keep the DOUT load small; above 35 pF, put 100 Ω in series with DOUT as close to the pin as practical.
